== Biography ==
=== Original will reviewed — 31 October 2026 ===
The readable continuation of Mary Glasgow’s will names her son John Glasgow to manage her property and gives a remainder to Mary Glasgow, described as the widow of deceased Wilson Glasgow, and her heirs. The will is dated 5 April 1822; the recorded probate is 14 October 1822. Mary’s existing Newberry family and the probate four days after her reported gravestone death make Mary, wife of James (Crosier-512), the compatible maintained account. The named son is compatible with John Glasgow-1146; the widow is compatible with Mary McCracken-3711, widow of Wilson Glasgow-1982. These identifications are family-context inferences, not additional relationship clauses.

The opening on manuscript page 489 runs below the framing of the inspected scan; the following page begins mid-clause. This is a partial reading, not a complete transcription or complete heir list. A Robert Glasgow witnesses the will and proves it; that role is not a statement that he is a son, and no exact Robert profile is assigned. The readable text neither supplies Mary’s birth surname nor identifies her parents. It does not name Tennessee Robert Glasgow-2769 as Archibald’s son or exclude an omitted heir. No father confidence, attachment, mother, vital field or duplicate decision changes.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:939L-J8SF-5R Newberry Will Book H, pp.489–490, Mary Glasgow will, 5 April 1822, probate 14 October 1822], FamilySearch images248–249; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:939L-J8SN-1Y clipped opening]. Original scans inspected31October2026; partial reading only.</ref>

Mary was born about 1737.  She passed away in 1822.

Mary is the niece of Rachel Wilson, James Glasgow's Mother. Mary Glasgow, along with 212 others, signed the register to "call" Rev. David Proudfit to the Cedar Spring Associate Reformed Presbyterian Church on March 1, 1797.

Robert S. Glasgow, Jr. and Ann Glasgow. Glasgow Genealogy.
